channel.title: UBC AI & Health Network - News
channel.description: News from the UBC AI & Health Network

item.title: Using AI to help capture patient voices can lead to improved health decisions
item.description: A new study published in PLOS Digital Health suggests that artificial intelligence (AI) can integrate patient voices into healthcare decision-making

item.title: Why Canada must urgently build AI models on Canadian data to improve patient care and relieve system strain
item.description: An op-ed in The Hill Times by Dr. Craig Earle, CEO, at the Canadian Partnership Against Cancer, and UBC AI and Health Network co-lead, Dr. Raymond Ng outlines the urgent need to develop AI models built on Canadian data.

item.title: UBC AI and Health Network Co-Lead Dr. Anita Palepu Nominated for a 2026 YWCA BC Women of Distinction Award
item.description: Congratulations to Dr. Palepu, who was nominated in the education, training and development category.

item.title: Harnessing AI for improved ovarian cancer care
item.description: UBC researchers are part of an international team awarded $2 million to study how AI can improve patient outcomes for ovarian cancer

item.title: UBC AI and Health Network funds 11 new projects advancing responsible AI-powered health research for B.C.
item.description: Eleven research projects have been funded through the inaugural UBC AI and Health Network Fellows Program, which supports researchers harnessing artificial intelligence (AI) to transform health research and improve patient care across B.C.

item.title: UBC AI and Health Network Co-Lead Dr. Raymond Ng showcases the promise of AI in health at Greater Vancouver Board of Trade Event
item.description: On October 15, 2025, Dr. Raymond Ng joined UBC President Benoit-Antoine Bacon and a panel of spinoff and industry leaders at the Greater Vancouver Board of Trade event, Building a Better World Together Through Purposeful Research Partnerships.

item.title: To pandemic preparedness and beyond: Accelerating novel antibody therapeutics through cross-border collaboration
item.description: The UBC AI & Health Network congratulates Network Member Dr. Sriram Subramaniam on a new cross-border collaboration with Boston-based Alloy Therapeutics, a partnership that combines AI and structural biology to accelerate the discovery of antibody therapeutics.

item.title: United in Diversity and UBC Empower Medical Data Sciences Leaders
item.description: We’re excited to announce that UBC in collaboration with United in Diversity and with support from Bio Farma and D&V Medika, successfully delivered the inaugural Demystifying AI in Healthcare course in Bali, Indonesia.

item.title: Welcome, Nabilah Chowdhury
item.description: We’re very pleased to welcome Dr. Nabilah Chowdhury as the new Director, Network Management, UBC AI and Health Network effective September 15, 2025.

item.title: Scientists discover high-risk form of endometrial cancer — and how to test for it — using AI
item.description: A discovery by researchers at the University of British Columbia promises to improve care for patients with endometrial cancer, the most common gynecologic malignancy.

item.title: Drug discovery at an atomic scale
item.description: UBC’s Dr. Sriram Subramaniam is using powerful cryo-electron microscopes to accelerate drug development for cancer, infectious diseases and more.
